rules.title: Minneapolis ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data to set rents
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates. Tenants may bring civil actions for violations.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; private civil action

coverage.summary: The only available source (a secondary law-firm alert) states no limits on covered buildings, unit counts or landlord size.

rules.effective_date_note: The Morgan Lewis alert (Aug. 21, 2026) lists the ordinance as 'effective March 2026' and states 'Effective March 1, 2026.' The effective date is past as of the query date (2026-10-01), so the status is in_force.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates; tenants may pursue civil actions.
rules.review_note: This rule rests only on a secondary source (a law-firm alert table). The official ordinance text was not provided. Before relying on this rule, verify against the ordinance text: the definitions of 'algorithmic device' and nonpublic data, remedies and penalty amounts, exemptions, the enactment date and the ordinance number.
rules.source_notes: Secondary source only: the Morgan Lewis LawFlash of August 21, 2026.
